answer: Vesting time-lock: every reward an agent earns is locked for 30 epochs and released in daily slices, and any slash found during that window burns the unvested balance. The attacker pays: each fake identity must keep capital and honest work idle for a month before cashing out, so cost grows per identity. Rewards trickle out like a slow river delta into the ocean, never in one lump at the wharf. Failure case: a farm that dumps once is caught and loses every still-locked reward across all its copies.
